signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-17 ppt-web-core websocket auth transport)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:94-101 — buildWebSocketUrl(base, token) appends the full JWT access token to the handshake URL as a query parameter: `url.searchParams.set('token', token)`. openConnection() (:369) then opens `new WebSocket(buildWebSocketUrl(this.url, token), ['ppt.v1'])`, so the raw bearer JWT rides in the WS connect URL on every (re)connect.

Why it is a real exposure vector: unlike request bodies or Authorization headers, full request URLs (including query strings) are routinely captured in places the token should never land — reverse-proxy / load-balancer / CDN access logs, APM traces, the browser's own history and devtools network panel, and any intermediary that logs the request line. A leaked access JWT is a bearer credential; anyone who reads it from a log can replay it until it expires. The code's own comment (websocket.ts:360-366, WebSocketContext.tsx:170-176) documents WHY the query param is used (browsers cannot set an Authorization header on the WS handshake, and the api-server WsQuery contract in ws_notifications.rs reads `?token=`), and the wss:// default protects the token ON THE WIRE — but neither addresses the residual at-rest log-capture risk, which persists even over TLS because the terminating proxy/server sees and can log the decrypted query string.

Suggested hardening (frontend + a small backend endpoint): replace the long-lived access JWT in the URL with a short-lived, single-use WS 'ticket' — client POSTs (with the normal Authorization header) to a `/ws/ticket` endpoint that returns an opaque nonce valid for ~30s and one connection; the WS URL then carries `?ticket=<nonce>` instead of the JWT, so a logged URL exposes only a spent/expired nonce. If a ticket endpoint is out of scope, the cheaper mitigation is a backend-side guarantee that the WS handshake query string is stripped/redacted from all access logs (proxy + app tracing). Filed MEDIUM: exploitability requires log/history access (not remote-unauthenticated) and is partly mitigated by short JWT TTL + wss://, but a bearer token in a URL is a well-established anti-pattern worth closing. Note the same `?token=` pattern likely exists in the reality-web and mobile WS clients and in the api-server WsQuery handler — a fix should sweep all WS-auth call sites together.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 mobile-rn NFCAccessController.addToWallet builds the Apple Wallet pass with a SCRAMBLED reverse-DNS passTypeIdentifier — 'pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access' — that does not match the project namespace three.two.bit.ppt, so it cannot match the Apple Developer Portal pass-type registration / provisioning profile the code's own comment requires)
evidence: NFCAccessController.ts:383 sets `passTypeIdentifier: 'pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access'` when constructing the WalletPass for `addToWallet(credentialId)` (the iOS Apple-Wallet building-access credential path, method at :358-391). The reverse-DNS body is SCRAMBLED: it reads `bit.two.three` where the project's canonical namespace is `three.two.bit`. Per root CLAUDE.md the package namespace is `three.two.bit.ppt` and the iOS bundle is `three.two.bit.ppt.management`; app.config.ts confirms this at :250 (`bundleIdentifier: 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'`) and :318 (`package: 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'`). A correct Wallet pass type identifier would be `pass.three.two.bit.ppt.access` (or `pass.three.two.bit.ppt.management.access`), NOT `pass.bit.two.three.ppt.access`.

Impact: Apple requires the passTypeIdentifier to be pre-registered in the Apple Developer Portal and to match an entitlement in the app's provisioning profile — the code's own comment at :382 says exactly this ('passTypeIdentifier must be configured in Apple Developer Portal and match the provisioning profile. See docs/ios-wallet-setup.md'). Because the string embeds a namespace that does not exist anywhere else in the project, `NativeWallet.addPass(...)` (:390) will fail for every iOS user attempting Add-to-Wallet on a building-access credential — the whole feature is dead on arrival unless someone also mis-registered the same typo in the portal (which would itself violate the reverse-DNS convention). This is a security-adjacent access-control feature (physical building entry via NFC-in-Wallet).

Grep-confirmed uniqueness of the typo: `grep -rn 'bit.two.three|two.three.bit|three.two.bit'` across frontend/apps/mobile shows the scrambled `bit.two.three` ordering appears ONLY at NFCAccessController.ts:383 — every other namespace literal in the app uses the correct `three.two.bit` order (app.config.ts:250/318, usePushNotifications.test.ts:61/67/95 appId 'three.two.bit.ppt.management'). This is an isolated transposition, not a project-wide alternate convention.

Landable frontend-only fix (single string constant, no native prebuild — verified by biome + tsc + jest-expo in CI): change NFCAccessController.ts:383 to `passTypeIdentifier: 'pass.three.two.bit.ppt.access'` (align the reverse-DNS body with app.config.ts bundle namespace), and confirm the same identifier is what docs/ios-wallet-setup.md instructs registering in the Apple Developer Portal. Confidence medium: the namespace mismatch vs the project convention is code-verified and unambiguous statically; the runtime add-to-wallet failure is inferred (the portal/provisioning config is not in the repo and cannot be executed in the cloud runner).

Please try again.')}`. The error IS surfaced (role='alert', styled), so this is not a silent-failure — it is a localization/UX gap: sk/cs/de users get an English/technical error string for a common failure (e.g. requesting a signature on an ineligible lease) instead of a translated message. This mirrors an established recurring class in the ppt-web-ui corpus (code-review-ppt-web-ui-emergency-dir-raw-err-message, code-review-ppt-web-ui-errorboundary-raw-message-prod) but is a distinct, previously-unmined instance in the leases feature (UC e-sign / lease signature flow).

Confidence MEDIUM: the raw-message branch is confirmed statically; the exact server message contents were not runtime-inspected. Fix (cloud-landable, ppt-web frontend): map known mutation error statuses to translated keys (t('leases.esign.errors.*')) and fall back to t('common.unknownError') rather than error.message, or run error.message through an i18n message-resolver.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-server portal-listings input validation)
evidence: The portal-owner listing WRITE path validates ONLY its enum-like string fields and leaves every numeric and required-text field unvalidated. `create_listing` (routes/portal_listings.rs:207) calls `validate_enum` for propertyType/transactionType/currency and nothing else; `update_listing` (routes/portal_listings.rs:317) adds `validate_enum("status", ...)` but likewise validates no numeric/text field. `price: Decimal` (CreatePortalListingRequest:106, UpdatePortalListingRequest:126) is passed straight into `create_portal_listing`/`update_portal_listing` (portal_listings.rs:239 / :344) with no lower-bound check, so a negative or zero price is accepted.

There is NO database backstop: migration 00049_create_listings.sql:39 declares `price DECIMAL(15, 2) NOT NULL` with NO CHECK constraint (grep for a `price >= 0` / `CHECK (price` on listings returns nothing; the only price-related CHECK in the tree is 00194's `alert_type` enum). The price-change trigger in 00063_reality_portal_professional.sql:100 even guards `CASE WHEN OLD.price > 0 ... ELSE 0`, implicitly acknowledging non-positive prices can exist. So a portal owner (authenticated PortalPrincipal — realtor / FSBO) can POST /api/v1/my/listings or PATCH /api/v1/my/listings/{id} with `price: -1` (or 0) and it is stored and then rendered on the PUBLIC reality-web portal. The reality-web price-display findings (code-review-reality-web-edit-price-zero #2026-09-06, sell-price-nan) are downstream symptoms of exactly this missing server-side guard — the backend is the correct place to reject it.

The same handler also skips emptiness/length validation on the REQUIRED text fields `title`, `street`, `city`, `postal_code` (all non-Option `String`, portal_listings.rs:104-112) and lower-bound validation on `size_sqm`/`rooms`/`floor`/`total_floors` — a whitespace-only title or a negative `size_sqm` is accepted (and `size_sqm` feeds the €/m² aggregation in routes/price_map.rs:164, `AVG(CASE WHEN size_sqm > 0 THEN price / size_sqm END)`, so a negative size silently drops the listing from the price map rather than erroring).

This is a genuine inconsistency, not a stylistic nit: the sibling public write paths in the SAME server validate their inputs thoroughly — the anonymous inquiry/contact path (handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:156 validate_contact: name 2-100 chars, email format, phone format, message 10-2000 chars) and the article-comment path (routes/articles.rs:450 empty + MAX_COMMENT_BODY_LEN). The portal-listing write path is the outlier that trusts the client.

Impact: MEDIUM. No auth bypass and no crash (Decimal arithmetic tolerates negatives), and ownership/RLS scoping is correct (create/update are gated on portal_owner_id/created_by). But an authenticated portal owner can persist semantically-invalid listing data (negative/zero price, empty title) that is served on the public portal and skews the public price-map aggregation. Confidence MEDIUM: the full path was traced statically (handler -> request struct -> repo call -> DB column) and the absence of a DB CHECK was confirmed against migration 00049; not runtime-exercised. Fresh vs backlog: no prior reality-server finding covers portal-listing input validation (prior ones: categories/suggestions i18n+stubs, slug-is-uuid, sso 401 conflation, mark-read swallow, saved-search/import limits, alert-drainer stub, inquiry-detail, watermark). Fix (reality-server-only, cargo-test verifiable): add a small `validate_listing_fields` guard in portal_listings.rs (reject price <= 0, size_sqm <= 0 when present, rooms/floors < 0, and trim-empty/over-length title/street/city/postal_code) called at the top of both create_listing and update_listing, mirroring InquiriesHandler::validate_contact; optionally also add a `CHECK (price > 0)` in a follow-up migration as defence-in-depth.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-web listing-detail ListingHeader formats the PRIMARY headline price with a locally-redefined formatPrice hardcoded to en-US, wrong for every sk/cs/de/pl/hu visitor)
evidence: ListingHeader.tsx:6-16 defines a module-local `formatPrice(price, currency)` that calls `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', ...)` on BOTH branches (the no-currency fallback at :9 and the currency branch at :11-14). The locale is hardcoded to 'en-US' regardless of the visitor's route locale. This formatter renders the listing-detail HEADLINE price at :50 (`<span className="price">{formatPrice(listing.price, listing.currency)}`) and the price-per-sqm at :54, so on the public, SEO-indexed listing-detail page a Slovak/Czech/German buyer sees US-formatted money (',' thousands, '.' decimals, '$'-style symbol placement) instead of `1 234 €` / `1.234 €`. This is the single most prominent money field on the page.

This is the same anti-pattern already filed for a SIBLING file on 2026-09-10 (code-review-reality-web-additionalinfo-hardcoded-en-us-price, AdditionalInfo.tsx) but ListingHeader.tsx is a DISTINCT, un-flagged file and is higher-impact (H1-adjacent headline price vs a secondary section). lib/format.ts header (:5-6) explicitly states it exists to replace scattered `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {...})` sites that 'produced visibly wrong output for the other five' locales, and exposes `formatPrice(value, locale, options)` (:48-59) that threads `bcp47(locale)` + defaults to EUR. ListingHeader bypasses it with an inline en-US copy.

The locale is trivially in scope: ListingHeader is a `[locale]` route section and already calls `useTranslations('listing')` at :19, so `useLocale()` from next-intl is available. Landable frontend-only fix: delete the local formatPrice and `import { formatPrice } from '@/lib/format'`, calling `formatPrice(price, locale, { currency })` (mirror ListingCard.tsx:106 which already does exactly this).

Reproduce (static): grep -n "'en-US'" components/listings/sections/ListingHeader.tsx -> :9 and :11; grep -n "lib/format" ListingHeader.tsx -> no import. Non-duplicate: verified against all 95 prior code-review-reality-web-* ids and the only prior 'ListingHeader' string match is in an unrelated 2026-08-19 mobile-native-kmp signal. Confidence medium: the en-US hardcode is code-verified statically; exact rendered glyphs depend on runtime Intl data, not run-confirmed.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-web PhotoGallery never resets selectedIndex when the photos prop changes; a stale index dereferences an out-of-bounds photo -> mainPhoto.url TypeError)
evidence: PhotoGallery.tsx:18 holds `const [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex] = useState(0)` but NOTHING resets or clamps it when the `photos` prop changes — there is no `useEffect([photos])` and no bounds guard. After the empty-array early return (:54), the code does `const mainPhoto = photos[selectedIndex]` (:89) and immediately dereferences `mainPhoto.url` (:100) and `mainPhoto.caption` (:100). The lightbox path is identical: `photos[selectedIndex].url` (:187) and `photos[selectedIndex].caption` (:190/:194). If a mounted instance ever receives a SHORTER `photos` array while `selectedIndex` points past its new end, `photos[selectedIndex]` is `undefined` and `.url` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` -> the whole client subtree of the listing-detail page crashes.

Trigger condition: the same PhotoGallery React instance is re-rendered with a shorter photos array while selectedIndex > photos.length-1. selectedIndex is advanced by the thumbnail buttons (:130 setSelectedIndex(index), up to 4) and the lightbox arrows / keyboard handlers (:29-33, :169, :215). Because Next.js App Router preserves client-component state across param-only navigations within the SAME dynamic segment, a listing-A(12 photos, user on thumb 5) -> listing-B(2 photos) client transition on `/[locale]/listings/[slug]` would reuse this instance with selectedIndex=4 and photos.length=2 -> crash.

Reachability caveat (why score_delta=1, not 2): a static sweep of the current listing-detail tree found NO in-page slug->slug client navigation today — ListingDetailContent.tsx:38 uses a plain `<a href="/listings">` (full reload) and renders no similar/related ListingCard links, and SearchBar's `router.push('/listings/${slug}')` (SearchBar.tsx:49) lives on index/home pages, not the detail page. So the crash is currently LATENT: the missing bounds guard is real and code-verified, but no live trigger path was confirmed. It becomes an immediate reachable crash the moment a 'similar listings' client `<Link>` (a common, expected addition) is placed on the detail page.

Landable frontend-only fix: clamp on read (`const mainPhoto = photos[Math.min(selectedIndex, photos.length - 1)]`) or reset via `useEffect(() => setSelectedIndex(0), [photos])`, and gate the lightbox derefs the same way. Non-duplicate: verified against all 95 prior code-review-reality-web-* ids; the only prior 'PhotoGallery' mention (2026-08-20 code-review-reality-web-listinggrid-empty-i18n) references it incidentally as a component that DOES use useTranslations, not for this bounds bug.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-11 reality-web AgencyListings table defines a local formatPrice hardcoded to en-US, wrong for sk/cs/de/pl/hu agency users)
evidence: AgencyListings.tsx:373-378 defines a component-local `formatPrice = (price, currency) => new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency, maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(price)` and renders it in the listings table price cell at :397 (`{formatPrice(listing.price, listing.currency)}`). Locale is hardcoded 'en-US', so every sk/cs/de/pl/hu agency user sees US-formatted money in their own listing-management table.

Third remaining occurrence of the en-US anti-pattern that lib/format.ts (:5-6, :48-59 `formatPrice(value, locale, options)` with bcp47) was built to eliminate — distinct from the 2026-09-10 AdditionalInfo finding and the ListingHeader finding in this same run. AgencyListings.tsx does NOT import lib/format (grep -n 'lib/format' -> none).

Scored 1 (lower than the ListingHeader headline price) because this is the AUTHENTICATED agency-management tool table, not the public SEO listing-detail page — smaller audience and lower brand exposure, though still a real locale-correctness defect.

Landable frontend-only fix: `import { formatPrice } from '@/lib/format'` and thread the route locale (add `useLocale()`; the component already uses `useTranslations('agencyListings')` so next-intl locale is in scope), calling `formatPrice(listing.price, locale, { currency: listing.currency })`. Non-duplicate: the two prior signals that mention 'AgencyListings' (2026-08-03 code-review-reality-web-agency-import-i18n about CsvImport, 2026-08-29 code-review-reality-web-listing-grid-empty-dup about EmptyState) reference it only incidentally and neither covers this en-US formatPrice.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/organizations/members.rs — the three org-membership mutation handlers (add_organization_member :206, update_organization_member :429, and the delete handler at :717) gate on a single coarse permission flag (`users:create` :275 / `users:update` :499 / `users:delete` :717) plus a role-belongs-to-org check (`r.organization_id == id` :305, `new_role.organization_id != org_id` :531). They are otherwise correctly tenant-scoped. But two standard org-RBAC guardrails are ABSENT.

(1) No privilege-ceiling / anti-escalation check: update_organization_member (:509-539) validates only that `req.role_id` exists and belongs to the org — it never compares the target role's privilege set against the acting admin's own. Any member holding `users:update` can therefore assign ANY role in the org, including one strictly more privileged than their own (e.g. a full owner/admin role), to another member OR to themselves (there is no `target_user_id != admin_user_id` self-guard on the update path, unlike the delete path at :717). If `users:update` is ever granted to a non-owner role, this is an in-org vertical privilege escalation. Fix: require the acting role's permission set to be a superset of the role being granted (grant-only-what-you-hold), and reject self-escalation.

(2) No last-owner protection: neither update_organization_member nor the delete handler checks the remaining owner/admin count before demoting (:576-585) or removing (:717+) a member. Nothing prevents the sole remaining owner from being demoted to a member role or removed, orphaning the organization with no one holding owner-tier permissions (no recoverable admin path). grep for `owner_count`/`last.owner`/`remaining` across members.rs returns 0 hits. Fix: before a demotion or removal that would drop the org's owner-tier membership count to zero, reject with 409 (e.g. LAST_OWNER).

Impact: authorization-completeness / defense-in-depth. Both are model-dependent (severity hinges on whether `users:update` is grantable to non-owner roles in the seeded role catalogue — confirm against the roles seed / role_repo before implementing); filed at MEDIUM confidence because the missing guards are confirmed by static read of the handler but the exploitability of (1) depends on the permission model, and (2) is a clear data-integrity gap regardless. Backend-only fix in members.rs (+ possibly a role_repo helper for privilege comparison and an owner-count query).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/multi_currency.rs:373-411 — the `Trigger exchange rate fetch from external source` handler is a STUB that reports success as if rates were fetched. Line 397-398 comment: `// In a real implementation, this would call external APIs (ECB, XE) / For now, we just log the attempt`; grep for ECB/XE/reqwest/http_client/fetch_rate/external in the file returns only the comment — there is no rate-provider call. The handler calls `log_rate_fetch(Some(org_id), config.exchange_rate_source, true, 0, None)` (:399-402) — hardcoding success=true, rate_count=0 — then returns HTTP 200 `{ "success": true, "message": "Exchange rate fetch initiated" }` (:407-411). A client (or the scheduler) cannot distinguish 'rates refreshed' from 'no-op stub'; downstream conversions keep using stale rates while the API reports a successful refresh.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/multi_currency.rs:406 — `let _ = s.multi_currency_repo.update_last_rate_update(org_id).await;` swallows the timestamp-write error entirely. On the success arm the handler still returns `success: true` even if this UPDATE failed, so `last_rate_update` can silently fail to advance (feeding an incorrect staleness signal to any cadence/staleness logic) with no error surfaced to the caller or logs. Contrast the sibling writes in the same handler (get_or_create_currency_config :390-395, log_rate_fetch :399/:413) which correctly `.map_err(...)` to 500.

Impact: LOW — correctness/observability smell on an org-scoped admin action. Two-part fix: (a) either wire the real ECB/XE fetch or make the stub's response honest (e.g. 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED / a `stub: true` flag) so callers don't treat it as a real refresh; (b) replace the `let _ =` at :406 with a `.map_err(...)` (or at minimum a `tracing::warn!` on Err) so a failed watermark write is surfaced. Confidence medium: stub behaviour and the swallow are confirmed by static read; whether any consumer actually relies on last_rate_update for staleness is inferred, not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/core.tsx:99-101 — the Home page 'Open dashboard' button routes with an exact-equality role check: `navigate(user?.role === 'manager' ? '/dashboard/manager' : '/dashboard/resident')`. This sends EVERY manager-equivalent role other than the bare 'manager' string — `org_admin`, `super_admin`, `technical_manager`, `property_manager` — to the RESIDENT dashboard instead of the manager dashboard.

The repo already has the single-source-of-truth helper `isManagerRole(role)` in routes/shared.tsx:48 (backed by `MANAGER_ROLES = ['manager','org_admin','super_admin','technical_manager','property_manager']`), and it is used elsewhere precisely to avoid this drift: App.tsx:127 `const isOperator = isManagerRole(user?.role)` gates the operator nav links, and the detail/workspace route wrappers gate on it too. Home's hand-rolled `=== 'manager'` is the outlier and contradicts that helper — an org_admin sees operator-only nav links (App.tsx) but the Home CTA drops them onto the resident dashboard.

Impact: MEDIUM — role-based mis-routing / UX-correctness for all non-'manager' operator roles (the most common operator role in a seeded org is typically org_admin, so this likely mis-routes the majority of operators). Fix: `navigate(isManagerRole(user?.role) ? '/dashboard/manager' : '/dashboard/resident')`, importing `isManagerRole` from '../shared' (already imported in this module's sibling files). Confidence medium: the wrong branch is confirmed by static read; the resident dashboard is still a reachable page so this is a correctness/UX defect rather than a crash.

Fix: call `setLayout(fresh)` alongside `writeCachedLayout(sid, screen, fresh)` in Phase 2 (guarded by the existing shape-check and `!cancelled`), so a first-time or post-change fetch is reflected without waiting for the next cold start.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/components/ReadingForm.tsx:85-90 — the shared numeric change handler coerces with `type === 'number' ? Number.parseFloat(value) || 0 : value`. Because `Number.parseFloat('')` is NaN and `NaN || 0` is 0, clearing a numeric input (or typing a partial/invalid entry) silently rewrites the field to 0 instead of leaving it empty or flagging validation — the user cannot present an empty numeric field, and a fat-fingered entry becomes a real 0 reading.

For a meter READING form this is a correctness/data-entry hazard: a submitted 0 reading is a valid-looking value that can corrupt consumption deltas, and the `|| 0` masks the difference between 'unset' and 'zero'. The OCR-accept path (handleOcrAccept, :138) sets a real number directly, so this only bites manual entry — but manual entry is the primary path when OCR is disabled or fails (the catch at :113-116 falls back to manual entry).

Impact: LOW — input-coercion correctness on a single form field. Fix: keep the raw string in state and validate/parse on submit (or use `value === '' ? '' : Number.parseFloat(value)` and reject NaN in the existing `errors` validation) rather than collapsing to 0. Confidence medium: the coercion is confirmed by static read; classified LOW as it is a manual-entry edge case guarded by downstream submit validation.
